newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Arthuis says lira ERM entry should not be hasty.
newsitem.headline: Arthuis says lira ERM entry should not be hasty.

text.p: French Finance Minister Jean Arthuis said on Monday that the European Union should not be too hasty in bringing the Italian lira back into the exchange rate mechanism (ERM).
He also said the eventual rate at which the lira re-joins should be "durable, equitable and sustainable."
"To be hasty on the re-entry (of the lira) would mean to take a risk...which would cause harm to the Italian and European authorities," Arthuis told reporters.
"The return has to take place at the right moment. The conditions have to met. The partity should be durable, equitable and sustainable," he said.
The lira is currently trading at around 994 lire to the German mark, still well short of its old level in the ERM.
Meanwhile, a senior EU monetary official said negotiations over the lira's re-entry might have to be taken among finance ministers.
Typically, the EU's monetary committee, comprised of national treasury and central bank officials, take decisions on the application of countries into the ERM.
